sampling_model.design: Known exact-uniform covariate law \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\) with independent sampling and replacement adjacency; this is a deliberate design-specific restriction rather than Kennedy et al.'s unknown bounded-density random-design model.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent causal records \(O_i=(Y_i,A_i,X_i)\) with bounded observed outcomes \(\lvert Y_i\rvert\le1\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with \(e_0\le\pi(X)\le1-e_0\), consistency, and armwise conditional exchangeability.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No data-dependent nuisance pilot is released. One ordered vector containing the first-order score and upper-triangular Gram blocks followed by their binomial-normalized pair corrections receives independent Laplace noise calibrated to its complete \(\ell_1\) replacement sensitivity.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives the nonprivate pointwise-CATE Hölder minimax lower rate over a model with bounded covariate density, while Theorem 2 gives a matching local-polynomial R-learner under additional design and nuisance-estimation conditions.
Theorems 1--3 and Sections 3--5 give pseudo-outcome oracle inequalities and local-polynomial CATE error bounds with nuisance-product remainders.
Theorem 6 proves an \(f\)-DP composition guarantee for the sample-split multi-stage CATE meta-algorithm, without a Hölder minimax utility rate.
Algorithm 1 and Theorem 2 use local Hájek projection thresholding to obtain central-private utility bounds for bounded-kernel U-statistics.
Theorems 1 and 3 turn expected-Hamming couplings into central-private Le Cam and Assouad testing lower bounds, including shared-mixture laws in the convex hulls.
The transport characterization in the main lower-bound section bounds private testing power through an optimal-transport problem between hypothesis laws.
Theorems 2.1, 3.4, and 4.4 establish matching pointwise Besov-regression rates up to logarithmic factors under heterogeneous distributed privacy.
Sections 1.2--1.3 introduce valid instance-adaptive output perturbation by calibrating noise to a smooth upper envelope of local sensitivity.
Theorems 1 and 3 give approximate-DP output perturbation for finite and functional queries from orthogonal two-stage CATE learners, without a pure-central Hölder pointwise minimax characterization.

body.tldr: On the deliberately restricted class with a known exact-uniform covariate law and bounded observed outcomes, pointwise CATE is a regression-functional hybrid whose pure-central privacy cost has two distinct scales. One second-order local estimator uses a single ordered release of first-order moments and upper-triangular pair corrections with a complete all-dataset sensitivity ledger, and a positive exact-uniform fuzzy family supplies the Hamming-transport converse. The resulting incremental price is \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}=\max\{(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)},(n^2\epsilon_n)^{-1/(1+d/\gamma+d/(\alpha+\beta))}\}\). This design-specific claim is not an extension to Kennedy et al.'s unknown bounded-density model. The bounds give the full decomposition whenever privacy leads or nuisance smoothness is above the nonprivate elbow; the open question is a stability transfer from the attained benchmark to the symbolic exact-uniform nonprivate minimax risk in the remaining privacy-inactive region.

project_justification.gap: Kennedy et al. establish nonprivate pointwise-CATE minimax theory under bounded-density random design and density-qualified attainability conditions, while private CATE papers establish algorithmic privacy guarantees without a pure-central Hölder pointwise minimax frontier. None determines the additional central-private price generated by the product of propensity and outcome-regression errors on a known exact-uniform causal law.
project_justification.niche: Exact uniformity is narrower than a bounded-density design and is load-bearing: it makes the local projection geometry deterministic and the probability of at least two observations in each equal-volume microcell public. The theorem applies directly to randomized benchmark studies that generate covariate locations from a public uniform law; deterministic uniform-grid studies are a fixed-design analogue, not a claim covered by the iid theorem.
project_justification.fill: A single \(p^2+3p\)-coordinate Laplace release contains the score block, the upper-triangular Gram block, and their two exact occupancy-normalized corrections; every subsequent symmetry and spectral operation is postprocessing. Boundedness is imposed only on observed outcomes, with causal and kernel bounds derived from consistency, armwise exchangeability, and overlap. A smooth positive exact-uniform fuzzy family supplies singleton cancellation and a componentwise Hamming coupling, while one open symbolic-risk transfer question remains separate from the queued nonprivate converse.

body.related_work: Kennedy et al. (2024), Theorem 1 and Remark 2, analyze a bounded-density random-design Hölder model; Theorem 2 and Appendix B.8 add design-estimation conditions for attainability. Their localized fuzzy hypotheses and higher-order local R-moment architecture inform this proposal, but their class is not a citation for known exact uniformity, and their lower construction does not settle the exact-uniform nonprivate risk used here. Kennedy (2023), Theorems 1--3 and Sections 3--5, gives pseudo-outcome oracle inequalities and local-polynomial error bounds, but risk control alone supplies no neighboring-record stability. Niu et al. (2022), Theorem 6, proves \(f\)-DP composition for a sample-split multi-stage CATE meta-algorithm without a Hölder minimax utility theorem. Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025), page 3 and Theorems 1 and 3, assume bounded observed outcomes and develop approximate-DP orthogonal two-stage CATE releases for finite or functional queries; they do not provide a pure-central Hölder pointwise minimax rate or the \(n^2\epsilon_n\) coupled-nuisance branch. Chaudhuri et al. (2024), Algorithm 1 and Theorem 2, stabilize bounded-kernel U-statistics using local Hájek projections; the exact-uniform binomial normalization here is a causal-specific construction. Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen (2024), Theorems 2.1, 3.4, and 4.4, establish pointwise Besov-regression rates under heterogeneous distributed privacy rather than one-database pure central privacy with causal nuisances. Acharya, Sun, and Zhang (2021), Theorems 1 and 3, and Lalanne, Garivier, and Gribonval (2023), the main transport reduction, supply private testing inequalities but no smooth causal shared-prior coupling. Nissim, Raskhodnikova, and Smith (2007), Sections 1.2--1.3, explain why typical occupancy cannot replace a worst-neighbor sensitivity certificate. Every comparator is used as methodological input and is downgraded to informed-by positioning.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact occupancy normalization and deterministic projection geometry require a known exact-uniform random design with equal public cell volumes. The theorem does not cover an unknown or merely bounded covariate density, and the stated iid result does not automatically cover a deterministic uniform grid. The upper theorem contains the explicit benchmark \(b_n\); replacing it by \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\) below the nuisance elbow and outside privacy-leading regimes is the stated open-ended question, not an assumed consequence of generic output perturbation.
body.honest_scope: The causal boundedness consequence, projection identity, pair sensitivity, fuzzy membership, component transport, upper envelope, lower envelope, and phase diagram are theorem obligations on the known exact-uniform class with bounded observed outcomes. The full symbolic decomposition is settled by those obligations for \(q\ge q_0\) and whenever \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\gtrsim b_n\). It remains open for \(q<q_0\) when privacy is inactive relative to \(b_n\). The queued exact-uniform nonprivate converse is neither cited as established nor duplicated. As a sanity reduction, fixing the nuisances removes the fuzzy branch and leaves the usual pointwise private-regression balance \(r_G\); letting privacy vanish leaves the nonprivate benchmark symbolic. Privacy sequences with \(\epsilon_n<n^{-1}\), unknown bounded-density designs, and deterministic fixed designs are outside the stated theorem; no saturation or design-transfer claim is made for those regimes.
